summary: A scene from a fiction book (Book 10, part 159) in which Leon is offered a 'strategic research' role by Brautigan, with Ria and Carmela present, and turns it down after noticing the job avoids the clients. He walks out, then meets a realtor who is selling his Lower East Side apartment, which he bought for two million dollars less than a year earlier; she warns that he will not recoup what he paid because the market has turned.
one_line: Leon rejects a comfortable but hollow job offer from Brautigan, then learns from a Lower East Side realtor that his two-million-dollar apartment is now worth less.
key_facts: Brautigan describes the proposed 'strategic research' job as figuring out what everyone is up to, putting people together, and proposing organizational structures for design and deployment.
Leon notes that Brautigan's description of the job never mentions the clients.
Leon realizes he holds power over Brautigan, Ria and Carmela in that moment, but he chooses not to exploit it.
Leon says 'Nice working with ya' and turns his back on what the note calls the sweetest, softest job anyone could ask for.
Leon says goodbye to Carmela with 'adios' and 'buena suerte' on his way out.
The realtor is young, no-nonsense, black, and grew up on the Lower East Side, and her advertising describes her as 'A local realtor for a local neighborhood.'
Leon paid two million dollars for the apartment less than a year before the realtor meeting.
The purchase used an 80 percent mortgage, and Ate underwrote it, bringing the interest rate down to less than two percent.
The apartment has a large corner picture window overlooking Broome Street and Grand Street.
The realtor says she wants the apartment to go to a real neighborhood resident rather than a developer or a corporate apartment broker renting to VIPs.
The realtor tells Leon he will not get what he paid, calling the claims 'They're not making any more Manhattan' and 'Location location location' lies.
The realtor says the market is designed to make buyers panic and overspend.
